levels.title: Plan a Reusable Sales Tracker
levels.objective: Choose the essential fields and business questions for a repeatable workbook.
levels.teaching: Start with the decision the tracker must support, then choose fields that can answer it. An order tracker needs a stable ID and clear dates, amounts and statuses.

challenges.prompt: A shop wants to track paid orders and monthly revenue. Which field set is fit for that goal?

options.a: Order ID, date, amount, payment status
options.b: Customer nickname and background color only
options.c: One merged text note per week

challenges.feedback: Order identifiers, dates, numeric amounts and payment status enable reconciled sales reports.

challenges.prompt: The manager asks for an order-level tracker but the sheet has only daily totals. What should you add?

options.a: A source-linked, individual order record for each sale

challenges.feedback: Order-level records preserve traceability and allow later aggregation and verification.

challenges.prompt: A well-designed order tracker can use a stable Order ID to reconcile records across weekly reports.
challenges.feedback: Stable identifiers allow comparisons and prevent counting the same order twice.

levels.title: Add Data Validation and Checks
levels.objective: Prevent common entry errors and spot inconsistent totals.
levels.teaching: Data validation constrains acceptable entries; check formulas detect errors after entry. Choose rules based on actual business requirements.

challenges.prompt: Order Status should be only New, Packed or Shipped. What validation setting fits?

options.a: A dropdown allowing those three values
options.c: A formula converting all statuses to Paid

challenges.feedback: A permitted-value dropdown prevents accidental variants and invalid states.

challenges.prompt: Someone enters Quantity = -4 on a new customer order. What is the most useful safeguard?

options.a: A positive-whole-number validation rule for normal orders
options.c: Leave the value because any integer is allowed

challenges.feedback: Quantity should follow defined business rules; returns/refunds need a separate documented process.

challenges.prompt: Validation rules mean you never need to review imported or pasted data for errors.
challenges.feedback: Imports and overrides can bypass or conflict with validation; reconciliation is still required.

levels.title: Add a Basic Expense View
levels.objective: Summarize monthly expenses by category and calculate a reasonable total.
levels.teaching: Expenses should be stored as individual transactions with category, date, amount and receipt reference. Use numeric totals to compare planned and actual spending.

challenges.prompt: Sample expenses are Rent PKR 20,000, Utilities 5,000, Packaging 2,000. What is the total monthly expense?
A repeated electricity bill reference appears twice in the sheet. What should happen before a monthly total is shared?

options.a: Check invoice/receipt records to determine whether one bill was entered twice
options.b: Ignore because the amounts are small

challenges.feedback: Expense totals require one entry per real transaction; investigate duplicates using source documents.

challenges.prompt: Money entries written as free text in an Expense Details column can be added accurately with SUM without any conversion.
challenges.feedback: Amounts need a numeric field; free-text descriptions should be kept separate.

levels.title: Share a Sheet Safely
levels.objective: Set read/edit access appropriately for synthetic and sensitive business data.
levels.teaching: Sharing should follow least privilege: viewers can inspect reports, editors can change records. Never expose real contact data in public links or learning exercises.

challenges.prompt: A partner only needs to read a finished report. Which access level is appropriate?

options.b: Viewer with the minimum required scope
options.c: Public link allowing anyone to edit

challenges.feedback: Viewer access satisfies read-only needs without granting unnecessary write permissions.

challenges.prompt: An order sheet includes real customer phone numbers. A teammate asks to publish it for a class. What should you do?

options.a: Use a fictional/anonymized dataset and restrict the original
options.b: Publish it unchanged because it helps learning
options.c: Hide the phone column visually but share the unrestricted file

challenges.feedback: Hiding a column is not anonymization or access control; use synthetic records instead.

challenges.prompt: Sharing a spreadsheet with Edit access is always required for someone who only needs to see monthly totals.
challenges.feedback: Read-only access is adequate for review and protects data integrity.

levels.title: Explain Insights in Plain Language
levels.objective: Write a concise factual interpretation and acknowledge data limitations.
levels.teaching: A useful summary names the metric, period, direction and magnitude, then distinguishes observed facts from possible explanations.

challenges.prompt: April revenue was PKR 90,000 and May revenue PKR 99,000. Which statement is accurate?

options.a: Revenue rose PKR 9,000, or 10%, between April and May
options.b: Revenue fell PKR 9,000 between April and May

challenges.prompt: A spreadsheet shows 10% higher revenue but no campaign data. Which claim should your written summary avoid?

options.a: Revenue was 10% higher than the prior month
options.b: A specific advertising campaign caused the increase
options.c: The report covers April and May

challenges.feedback: Without evidence for causation, you can report the measured change but not its cause.

challenges.prompt: Including a note that refunds were not included helps readers interpret a revenue comparison correctly.
challenges.feedback: A clearly stated exclusion prevents a reader from mistaking gross transaction totals for net retained revenue.

levels.title: Capstone: Deliver the Tracker
levels.objective: Self-check an accurate sales/expense workbook and communicate limitations.
levels.teaching: A complete handover contains a clean dataset, reliable formulas, a meaningful chart, an interpretation and safe sharing settings. Verify each part with a clear rubric.

challenges.prompt: Which set of outputs makes the mock sales tracker genuinely useful?

options.a: A clean source table, checked formulas, a labeled chart, two KPIs and a limitation note
options.b: A logo image and a total typed by hand
options.c: Only a colorful chart without source values

challenges.feedback: The capstone checks both the operational data and the clarity of its interpretation.

challenges.prompt: Your calculated total is PKR 2,700 but a source-ledger subtotal is PKR 2,900. What should you do before submitting the project?

options.a: Reconcile the difference and note unresolved issues rather than force a match
options.c: Hide the source sheet and publish the chart

challenges.feedback: A responsible handover verifies discrepancies before presenting outcomes as correct.

challenges.prompt: A capstone may be marked accurate even when formulas are broken, provided the chart looks polished.
challenges.feedback: Presentation quality cannot substitute for correct underlying data and reproducible calculations.
